key_insight: Local atomic-swap tests indicate that GNN feature rankings can retain physically meaningful neighbor-shell information even under deliberate overfitting.
engineering_relevance: Perturbation-based validation can help engineers assess whether materials-model explanations reflect local chemistry rather than compositional artifacts.
method: Deliberately overfit a physics-aware GNN ensemble to DFT-derived decomposition enthalpies for three CoMoFeNiCu stoichiometries.
Constrain output weights to encode feature importance.
Swap individual atomic sites and re-rank features to test spatial sensitivity.
evidence_signal: Using approximately 900 binary and 4,500 ternary decomposition pathways, the study observed attribution changes with spatial decay consistent with the GNN interaction cutoff.
watch_item: Validation is limited to one alloy system and three stoichiometries; generalization across chemistries remains untested.
paper_title: Validating Graph Neural Network Feature Attribution Through Local Perturbations: A Study on CoMoFeNiCu Decomposition Enthalpy
